metadata.title: Seedance Video-to-Video & Video Editing Guide
metadata.description: Learn how Seedance video-to-video and editing workflows use reference clips for motion, style, background, camera, green screen, and scene changes.

hero.title: Seedance Video-to-Video
hero.description: A practical Seedance video to video guide for preparing a reference clip, writing an edit prompt, preserving motion, changing style, and checking the final result.
hero.tip: Video-to-video support varies by model and provider. Confirm the selected mode, file requirements, input rights, and output limits before uploading a clip.

introduce.title: What Seedance video-to-video can control
introduce.description: A reference clip can provide motion and timing, while a prompt directs the intended transformation. State the relationship instead of asking for a vague “better” video.

items.title: Motion and blocking
items.description: Preserve the actor’s movement, camera path, pose sequence, or object trajectory when those are the reason for using the clip.

items.title: Style and environment
items.description: Change visual language, lighting, materials, or setting while describing which motion and identity attributes must remain.

items.title: Editing and replacement
items.description: Name the background, subject, prop, or time segment to modify and explain how the replacement should interact with light and motion.

items.title: Quality and delivery
items.description: Check frame continuity, faces, hands, product geometry, audio sync, dimensions, watermark, and file format.

benefits.title: Seedance video editing patterns
benefits.description: These patterns cover Seedance video to video, green-screen, background replacement, style transfer, and provider-specific searches such as Seedance 2.5 video inpaint.

items.title: Keep motion, change setting
items.description: Use the clip for blocking and timing, then describe the new environment, lighting, camera, and physical interaction.

items.title: Keep subject, change background
items.description: Specify the replacement scene and how shadows, reflections, hair, clothing, and perspective should respond.

items.title: Edit a time window
items.description: Identify the target timestamp or segment, state the edit, and define continuity before and after the change.

items.title: Extend from the ending
items.description: Describe the next action and camera movement from the last frame, then check whether the provider exposes video extension.

features.title: A safe video-to-video workflow
features.description: Use a short source clip and one intended transformation first; complexity can be added after the baseline is stable.

items.title: 1. Own or license the source
items.description: Confirm that you can upload and transform the people, footage, music, logos, and locations in the clip.

items.title: 2. Inspect the source
items.description: Note frame rate, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, camera path, faces, text, and audio.

items.title: 3. Define invariants
items.description: State what must stay: identity, motion, composition, timing, voice, or product geometry.

items.title: 4. Describe one edit
items.description: Name the replacement or style change, time window, lighting response, and desired ending.

items.title: 5. Run a short test
items.description: Use the smallest accepted clip and inspect transitions before using a longer source.

items.title: 6. Compare the output
items.description: Review the source and result side by side for drift, artifacts, sync, rights, and delivery quality.

faq.title: Seedance Video-to-Video FAQ
faq.description: Clear answers for the most common Seedance searches and workflows.

items.question: Does Seedance 2.0 support video to video?
items.answer: Supported Seedance 2.0 surfaces can expose reference-video and video-to-video workflows. Check the selected model and interface for current input rules.

items.question: Can Seedance edit an existing video?
items.answer: Some Seedance versions and providers support editing, extension, or reference-based transformation. Describe the exact edit and confirm the mode before uploading.

items.question: Can I change a video’s style with Seedance?
items.answer: Use the source video for motion or blocking and state the target style, materials, lighting, and constraints. The output remains probabilistic, so test a short clip first.

items.question: Can Seedance replace a green-screen background?
items.answer: Seedance 2.5 official materials describe green-screen editing, while actual access depends on the provider. Use authorized footage and specify the lighting and perspective of the new scene.

items.question: Why do frames drop or flicker in video-to-video?
items.answer: Long or complex sources, ambiguous edits, fast camera movement, and too many simultaneous changes can reduce continuity. Simplify the clip and isolate one transformation.

items.question: Can I use a reference video of a real person?
items.answer: Only with the person’s authorization and within the provider’s real-person and likeness rules. A public clip is not automatically safe to transform.

cta.title: Make one controlled edit first
cta.description: Use a rights-cleared source clip, name the invariant and the edit, and inspect the transition before scaling the workflow.
